endorsements.title: Considerations for the regulation of generative AI-enabled medical devices (discussion paper)
endorsements.quote: Relevant testing may include differential diagnosis generation assessed for completeness and appropriate prioritization of serious diagnoses, multi-turn simulated encounters scored for the quality and sequencing of follow-up questions, and scenarios designed to detect premature diagnostic closure in which initially benign information masks a more serious underlying condition.

endorsements.title: Artificial Intelligence-Enabled Device Software Functions: Lifecycle Management and Marketing Submission Recommendations (draft guidance)
endorsements.quote: When deploying adversarial training techniques, sponsors should be cognizant of the 1467 trade-offs that may arise between enhanced robustness to attacks and the potential 1468 negative impact on model performance (e.g., accuracy), and provide information on how 1469 the trade-offs are managed.

endorsements.title: FUTURE-AI: international consensus guideline for trustworthy and deployable artificial intelligence in healthcare
CHAI Responsible AI Guide (Assurance Standards Guide)
endorsements.quote: The team should ascertain whether the AI solution has undergone thorough robustness testing, and whether this process and its outcomes have been documented.

endorsements.title: Health Equity Across the AI Lifecycle (HEAAL) framework
endorsements.issuer: Health AI Partnership; PLOS Digital Health (PMID 38723025, doi:10.1371/journal.pdig.0000390)
endorsements.quote: The assessment of reliability and validity ensures that the solution consistently achieves pre-specified performance targets across technical and clinical measures.

endorsements.title: Towards quality management of artificial intelligence systems for medical applications
endorsements.quote: This could be e.g. a user-specific test data set that includes adversarial examples, randomly generated data, corrupted or otherwise faulty input.

endorsements.title: Toward Clinical Generative AI: Conceptual Framework
endorsements.quote: Researchers should make responsible use of AI; use standardized reporting guidelines [ 58 ]; systematically compare different types of AI-based tools; evaluate the accuracy, repeatability, and reproducibility of the tools; and incorporate ethical and legal considerations.

endorsements.title: Increasing acceptance of AI-generated digital twins through clinical trial applications
endorsements.quote: Because missing data are so prevalent in many healthcare applications, it is also important to test how robust a model's performance is to missing inputs.

endorsements.title: Bridging the gap: a practical step-by-step approach to warrant safe implementation of large language models in healthcare
endorsements.quote: When deployed in clinical practice, LLM responses need to be reproducible and stable over time, ensuring reliability in their outputs.

endorsements.title: Recommendations for Successful Development and Implementation of Digital Health Technology Tools
endorsements.quote: This can include measuring model performance consistency across different patient subgroups, assessing model interpretability through techniques like feature importance analysis, stress testing with out-of-distribution inputs, and systematic evaluation of error rates and their clinical implications using standardized benchmarking datasets [ 42 43 ].

endorsements.title: Rethinking scale in ophthalmic artificial intelligence: from bigger models to smarter clinical reasoning
endorsements.quote: Such evaluation paradigms may require moving beyond static test sets toward stress testing under domain shift, longitudinal consistency analysis, and human-AI interaction studies that assess decision support quality rather than prediction accuracy alone.

endorsements.title: Safeguarding AI-driven digital health - An adaptation of the Swiss cheese model for safety
endorsements.quote: Model development, evaluation and change control - Oversimplified model - Poor calibration - Weak search algorithm - NLP limitations - Algorithmic failure - Model performance evaluation beyond accuracy - Calibration assessment - Task-specific validation - Stress testing under edge cases

endorsements.title: The VIBE-HI framework: a conceptual model for evaluating vibe coding appropriateness, quality, and safety in health informatics
endorsements.quote: Hallucination Resilience (HR) is the demonstrated capacity of the artefact to fail safely when the model has fabricated APIs, packages, or logic, tested through adversarial prompting, dependency verification against trusted registries, and runtime checks on critical paths.

endorsements.title: Subcategorisation of Data for AI Models in Healthcare: A Case Study in Mammography
endorsements.quote: We argue that it is important to test any model fully on available categories alongside a sensitivity analysis before deployment.

endorsements.title: Empowering Educators to Build AI Chatbots in Health Professions Education: Tutorial on a No-Code Design Workflow
endorsements.quote: Common failure modes to anticipate and test for include excessive unprompted disclosure of information, inaccurate disciplinary content, feedback that is too vague or poorly anchored to learning objectives, and persona inconsistency across extended interactions.

evidence.title: Preserving Informative Presence: How Missing Data and Imputation Strategies Affect the Performance of an AI-Based Early Warning Score
evidence.outcome: Missing-input and imputation stress testing
evidence.effect: Mean imputation decreased AUROC from 0.918 to 0.883; MICE declined further to 0.827.
evidence.quote: When missing values were imputed using values randomly drawn from within one SD of the mean observed values for the corresponding non-event and event groups, the AUROC decreased to 0.883 (95% CI: 0.875–0.891) compared with 0.918 (95% CI: 0.912–0.924) under the model’s default normal-value imputation method (DeLong test, p < 0.001).

evidence.title: Deep learning approach for stroke volume variation estimation: retrospective modeling and prospective deployment in real-world practice
evidence.outcome: Robustness to noisy arterial pressure signals, by signal quality index
evidence.effect: SVVNet was more robust to signal noise than the ABP-PWA algorithm (MAE 4.33 vs 30.87).
evidence.quote: It was more robust to signal noise (MAE = 4.33 vs 30.87).

evidence.title: ChatGPT-assisted pain history-taking system for musculoskeletal rehabilitation: Development and preliminary psychometric validation
evidence.outcome: Reproducibility of outputs across three repeated retests under controlled conditions
evidence.effect: Item-level repeatability perfect (agreement 100%; PABAK = 1.00); response-level agreement 94-100%; PABAK 0.89-1.00.
evidence.quote: Item-level repeatability was perfect (agreement, 100%; PABAK = 1.00), and response-level repeatability was near-perfect (agreement, 94-100%; PABAK = 0.89-1.00).

evidence.title: Automated Post-Analytical Workflow for Newborn Screening Using a Hybrid Rule-Based and Retrieval-Augmented Large Language Model System
evidence.outcome: Reproducibility of diagnostic conclusions across repeated generation from identical inputs
evidence.effect: 50 drafts generated from identical inputs produced stable diagnostic conclusions.
evidence.quote: Repeated generation from identical inputs (50 drafts) produced stable diagnostic conclusions, and all source-attributed statements cited correct sources, with 56 of 60 fully covered by the cited excerpt.
evidence.sample_unit: synthetic cases (report drafts reviewed by 5 specialists)

evidence.title: VeriSim: A Configurable Framework for Stress-Testing Medical AI Under Patient Communication Noise
evidence.outcome: Diagnostic accuracy and conversation length under simulated patient communication noise versus clean cases
evidence.effect: Realistic noise reduced diagnostic accuracy by 15-25 percentage points and increased conversation length by 34-55%; 7-8B models degraded 1.4x more than 70B+ models.
evidence.quote: Across seven open-weight LLMs, realistic noise reduces diagnostic accuracy by 15-25 percentage points and increases conversation length by 34-55%; the 7-8B models degrade 1.4x more than 70B+ models.

evidence.title: Structured Visual Evidence Decomposition for Evidence-Grounded Multimodal Screening of Obstructive Sleep Apnea-Hypopnea Syndrome
evidence.outcome: Effect of seven-question visual decomposition and balanced adjudication ablations on screening performance
evidence.effect: Ablations showed that seven-question visual decomposition and balanced final adjudication were critical to the high-sensitivity operating point; the full framework outperformed clinical-only, direct multimodal, and naive two-stage pipelines.
evidence.quote: Ablations showed that seven-question visual decomposition and balanced final adjudication were critical to the high-sensitivity operating point.

evidence.title: Automated Suicide Risk Factor Monitoring in Crisis Text Line Users: Comparative Study of AI and Human Ratings Using Large Language Models
evidence.outcome: LLM rating reliability across repeated runs, temperature settings and prompting styles
evidence.effect: Zero-shot prompting at temperature 0 yielded perfect inter-rating reliability (α=1.00, 95% CI: [1-1] for high & very high risk); lower temperatures consistently improved reliability and accuracy.
evidence.quote: Zero-shot prompting at temperature 0 yielded perfect inter-rating reliability (α=1.00, 95% CI: [1-1] for high & very high risk), while few-shot prompting showed best human-AI agreement for very high risk (α=0.78, 95% CI: [0.67-0.89]) and strongest classification performance (balanced accuracy 0.54-0.71).

evidence.title: Large-Language-Model Mortality Risk Stratification in the Intensive Care Unit: A Benchmark Against APACHE II
evidence.outcome: Consistency of LLM risk stratification across repeated evaluations
evidence.effect: Gemini, GPT-4, and R1 showed highest consistency across repeated evaluations; Llama showed greater variability that improved with added context.
evidence.quote: Gemini, GPT-4, and R1 exhibited the highest consistency across repeated evaluations, while Llama showed greater variability that improved with context.

evidence.title: Performance assessment of large language models in cancer staging: Comparative analysis of Mistral models
evidence.outcome: Test-retest reproducibility of LLM cancer staging across repeated runs
evidence.effect: Kappa > 0.95 for Mistral Large and Medium; top models test–retest reliability exceeding 97%; smaller and locally deployed models lacked robustness, especially unit conversions and complex staging rules.
evidence.quote: The top-performing models had a test–retest reliability exceeding 97%, while smaller models and locally deployed versions lacked sufficient robustness, particularly in handling unit conversions and complex staging rules.

evidence.title: New Model, Old Risks? Sociodemographic Bias and Adversarial Hallucinations Vulnerability in GPT-5
evidence.outcome: Adoption of fabricated medical detail
evidence.effect: GPT-5 adopted or elaborated on the fabrication in 65% of runs, versus 53% for GPT-4o.
evidence.quote: Additionally, in an adversarial re-run that inserted one fabricated medical detail into otherwise standard clinical cases, GPT-5 adopted or elaborated on the fabrication in 65% of runs (vs 53% for GPT-4o).
evidence.sample_unit: physician-validated emergency vignettes (each replayed across 32 sociodemographic labels plus control)

evidence.title: Gender-Based Prompt Variation and Diagnostic Accuracy of Large Language Models in Chagas Disease and Visceral Leishmaniasis: A Comparative Experimental Study
evidence.outcome: Diagnostic accuracy change under prompt variation (male vs female physician persona)
evidence.effect: Female prompt gave numerically higher VL accuracy in all four models (8.3–16.7 points gain); no between-prompt differences statistically significant (all p>0.05).
evidence.quote: No between-prompt differences reached statistical significance (all p>0.05).

evidence.title: Physician Facing AI Tools Show Distinct Failure Modes Under Structured Stress Testing
evidence.outcome: Critical element capture under perturbed inputs (anchoring, cognitive load, social conformity, incorrect directive)
evidence.effect: Anchoring and social conformity pressure reduced critical element capture on both platforms; cumulative stressor burden reduced capture only on OpenEvidence. ChatGPT captured 81.4% vs OpenEvidence 61.0%.
evidence.quote: Anchoring and social conformity pressure were associated with reduced critical element capture across both platforms, while cumulative stressor burden reduced critical element capture only on OpenEvidence.
evidence.sample_unit: responses (to 1920 prompts across 60 simulated critical care vignettes)

evidence.title: Characterizing Documented Psychosocial Stressors in Pediatric Psychiatric Emergencies with an Open-Weight Large Language Model
evidence.outcome: Reproducibility of LLM classifications across 50 repeated calls per note and its relation to human agreement
evidence.effect: Mean LLM-human agreement rose from 42.6% for classifications with <80% stability to 82.7% for 100% stability (Pearson r=0.36).
evidence.quote: Stability was associated with human agreement: mean LLM-human agreement increased from 42.6% for classifications with <80% stability to 82.7% for 100% stability (Pearson r=0.36).
evidence.sample_unit: intake notes (parseable LLM outputs); 50 notes in human-rater validation

evidence.title: Uncertainty-aware extraction of clinical findings from Finnish EHRs using open large language models
evidence.outcome: Output reproducibility across repeated runs and temperatures, measured as entropy across 15 calls
evidence.effect: Each model-target combination was run 15 times (five temperatures × three repeats); entropy across calls flagged likely errors, with higher entropy in misclassified cases (2.4–3.4 times).
evidence.quote: Each combination received 15 calls (five temperatures × three repeats).

evidence.title: Schema-enforced large language model framework for sarcoma tumor board simulation: a methodology development and reproducibility pilot study
evidence.outcome: Decision-code reproducibility across three repeated runs of the same case under schema enforcement
evidence.effect: Overall reproducibility was 93.9% (1,006/1,071 decision-code instances stable); 17 cases (33.3%) had 100% reproducibility; reconstruction decision least stable (74.5%).
evidence.quote: Overall reproducibility was 93.9% (1,006 / 1,071 decision-code instances stable).
evidence.sample_unit: de-identified sarcoma cases (each run three times)

evidence.title: A Neuro-Symbolic Knowledge Graph and Large Language Model Hybrid Architecture for Multi-Modality Mental Health Counseling
evidence.outcome: Repeatability of KG decisions across repeated runs
evidence.effect: Decisions were 99.1% repeatable, 100% reconstructable per turn, and 100% provenance-auditable across all 354 KG nodes.
evidence.quote: Decisions were 99.1% repeatable, 100% reconstructable per turn, and 100% provenance-auditable across all 354 KG nodes.

evidence.title: Large language models for accurate disease detection in electronic health records
evidence.outcome: LLM performance robustness across model parameters and prompt structure
evidence.effect: LLM framework performed well over a wide range of parameter values.
evidence.quote: The LLM framework performed well over a wide range of parameter values.

evidence.title: The Impact of Acoustic and Informational Noise on AI-Generated Clinical Summaries
evidence.outcome: Scribe summary accuracy under acoustic noise, microphone distance and informational noise perturbations
evidence.effect: Errors, mainly omissions, rose for all noise types and levels; all facts omitted at 4.5 m; toddler and heavy rain caused 7 and 15 omissions at 0 and +5dB; informational noise largely rejected.
evidence.quote: Error rates and absolute error counts increased for all noise levels and noise types; the principal error being omissions.

evidence.title: Brain tumour segmentation with incomplete imaging data
evidence.outcome: Segmentation accuracy (Dice) with missing MRI sequences versus complete set
evidence.effect: Dice 0.907 (single sequence) to 0.945 (complete set) for whole tumours; 0.701 to 0.891 for component tissue types; models trained on incomplete data often equivalent to full-data models.
evidence.quote: We demonstrate that models trained on incomplete data can segment lesions very well, often equivalently to those trained on the full completement of images, exhibiting Dice coefficients of 0.907 (single sequence) to 0.945 (complete set) for whole tumours and 0.701 (single sequence) to 0.891 (complete set) for component tissue types.

evidence.title: Is ChatGPT a trusted source of information for total hip and knee arthroplasty patients?
evidence.outcome: Reproducibility of output quality across repeated runs of the same question
evidence.effect: No significant differences between repeated asks in accuracy (p=0.415), comprehensiveness (p=0.171), acceptability (p=0.176), and FKGL (p=0.793).
evidence.quote: There was no statistically significant difference in FKGL (t = 0.264; p = 0.793) between the first question responses (12.25; 95% CI 11.29 to 13.20) and the second question responses (12.06; 95% CI 11.02 to 13.10).

evidence.title: Use of a large language model with instruction-tuning for reliable clinical frailty scoring
evidence.venue: Journal of the American Geriatrics Society
evidence.outcome: Reproducibility of CFS scores across repeated runs, basic vs instruction-tuned prompt with temperature control
evidence.effect: Instruction-tuned prompt showed high inter-rater reliability (Fleiss' Kappa 0.887) and consistent responses in all scenarios; score distributions differed significantly from the basic prompt in five of seven scenarios.
evidence.quote: The instruction-tuned prompt showed high inter-rater reliability (Fleiss' Kappa of 0.887) and produced consistent responses in all scenarios.

evidence.title: Use of Generative AI to Identify Helmet Status Among Patients With Micromobility-Related Injuries From Unstructured Clinical Notes
evidence.outcome: Test-retest reproducibility of LLM helmet-status classification across 5 new chat sessions and days
evidence.effect: LLM did not perfectly replicate analyses across sessions and days (Fleiss κ = 0.91 across 5 trials; P < .001); it consistently replicated its hallucinations.
evidence.quote: The LLM did not perfectly replicate its analyses across new sessions and days (Fleiss κ = 0.91 across 5 trials; P < .001).

evidence.title: Addressing the implementation challenge of risk prediction model due to missing risk factors: The submodel approximation approach
evidence.outcome: Robustness to missing inputs and heterogeneity
evidence.effect: Across 1000 simulations per scenario, preconditioning and imputation were stable; OSS rMSPE increased under heterogeneous means.
evidence.quote: Under the heterogeneous mean scenarios ( Figure 3A ), rMSPEs from preconditioning-based submodels and the imputation approach are quite stable, whereas rMSPEs from OSS-based submodels increase with the heterogeneity in mean.

evidence.title: Large language model triaging of simulated nephrology patient inbox messages
evidence.outcome: Reproducibility of LLM triage across repeated runs two weeks apart
evidence.effect: Internal agreement of ChatGPT responses was 92% with intra-rater Kappa of 0.88.
evidence.quote: The internal agreement of ChatGPT responses was 92% with an intra-rater Kappa score of 0.88.

evidence.title: Optimizing ChatGPT's Interpretation and Reporting of Delirium Assessment Outcomes: Exploratory Study
evidence.outcome: Reproducibility of scores and reasoning across repeated ChatGPT runs on the same vignette
evidence.effect: Total scores varied less across ChatGPT trials than between human experts for most vignettes; ChatGPT-3.5 ranged 10-15 on vignette 4. Cited sentences sometimes varied despite identical totals.
evidence.quote: Interestingly, while the ChatGPT models may assign the same total score across multiple trials of the same vignette, the sentences from the vignette used to justify its decisions sometimes varied (see Multimedia Appendix 3 for more details).
evidence.sample_unit: trials per model (5 vignettes x 5 trials each)

evidence.title: Advancing personalized medicine in digital health: The role of artificial intelligence in enhancing clinical interpretation of 24-h ambulatory blood pressure monitoring
evidence.outcome: Reproducibility of ChatGPT ABPM interpretations across two rounds three months apart
evidence.effect: Agreement between rounds was 81% hypertension, 85% nocturnal hypertension, 89% nocturnal dipping, 94% abnormal heart rate; no significant accuracy difference between rounds (all p > 0.05); Kappa 0.63-0.76.
evidence.quote: The percentage agreement between the first and second round of ChatGPT's analysis was 81% in identifying hypertension, 85% in nocturnal hypertension, 89% in nocturnal dipping, and 94% in abnormal heart rate.

evidence.title: Retrieval augmented generation for 10 large language models and its generalizability in assessing medical fitness
evidence.outcome: Reproducibility of GPT-4 international RAG outputs across repeated runs
evidence.effect: Reproducibility score 4.86/5 over 4 repeats; IRR 0.93 for fitness prediction, 0.96 for healthcare-team instructions, 0.92 for optimization types.
evidence.quote: The S.C.O.R.E (Safety, Consensus, Objectivity, Reproducibility, Explainability) evaluation showed that the GPT4 RAG model was able to have high reproducibility of results (4.86 out of 5) and provided safe instructions (4.93 out of 5) (Supplementary Table 7 ).
evidence.sample_unit: clinical scenarios (3234 LLM responses vs 448 human responses)

evidence.title: Sensitivity of a deep-learning-based breast cancer risk prediction model
evidence.outcome: Sensitivity of predicted breast cancer risk to simulated image alterations (translation, rotation, cropping, pectoral removal)
evidence.effect: Model sensitive to translation, rotation, registration, cropping (LOA up to ±0.1); complete pectoral removal caused bias (1-yr LOA [-0.07, 0.04]); AUC unchanged (1-yr 0.90, 5-yr 0.77); left-right swap no impact.
evidence.quote: The model was sensitive to translation, rotation, registration, and cropping, where LOAs of up to ±0.1 were observed.

evidence.title: ChatGPT-4o-Generated Exercise Plans for Patients with Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus-Assessment of Their Safety and Other Quality Criteria by Coaching Experts
evidence.outcome: Effect of prompt detail on plan quality and safety ratings across three prompts
evidence.effect: Safety ratings by prompt: Prompt 1 4L/3M/2S, Prompt 2 2L/2M/5S, Prompt 3 3L/2M/4S; more detailed prompts gave minimal safety improvement, and quality improved in some training criteria.
evidence.quote: Using more detailed prompts (Prompts 2 and 3) generally resulted in minimal quality improvement ( Figure 1 , Prompt 1: 4× L, 3× M, 2× S, Prompt 2: 2× L, 2× M, 5× S, Prompt 3: 3× L, 2× M, 4× S)

evidence.title: Comparative performance of large language models in structuring head CT radiology reports: multi-institutional validation study in Japan
evidence.outcome: Effect of prompting strategy and repeated-run reproducibility on classification accuracy
evidence.effect: Claude and GPT stable across prompts; Gemini significantly higher with Chain of Thought than Standard or Self Consistency. Each combination run three times; reproducibility compared across runs.
evidence.quote: For both intracranial hemorrhage and skull fracture classification, Claude and GPT maintained relatively consistent accuracy across different prompting methods, whereas Gemini achieved significantly higher accuracy with Chain of Thought prompting than with either Standard or Self Consistency prompting.
evidence.sample_unit: head CT radiology reports (one per patient)

evidence.title: Patient Triage and Guidance in Emergency Departments Using Large Language Models: Multimetric Study
evidence.outcome: Run-to-run consistency (Kendall correlation) of MEWS scoring across 10 repeated runs, before vs after prompt engineering
evidence.effect: GPT-4-Turbo mean Kendall coefficient improved from 0.6176 (SD 0.2135) to 1.00 (SD 0); GPT-4o improved from 0.8327 to 0.8646 (not significant, P=.32).
evidence.quote: For GPT-4-Turbo, the mean value dramatically improved from 0.6176 (SD 0.2135) in trial 1 to 1.00 (SD 0) in trial 2.
evidence.sample_unit: simulated patient scenarios (MEWS triage); 264 scenarios for department guidance

evidence.title: Impact of analytical bias on machine learning models for sepsis prediction using laboratory data
evidence.outcome: SVM sepsis model AUC under simulated analytical biases in WBC, PLT, ESR inputs
evidence.effect: Original AUC 90.6%; across 26 bias conditions AUC ranged down to 87.8% for combined biases; no statistically significant differences (p>0.05), though bias can influence performance depending on parameters and combinations.
evidence.quote: No statistically significant differences were observed for AUC (p>0.05).

evidence.title: Leveraging ChatGPT for improved decision-making in interfacility transfers for plastic surgery emergencies based on United States guidelines
evidence.outcome: Effect of prompt phrasing on guideline alignment and error direction of transfer recommendations
evidence.effect: Primer 1 and 3 had 77% alignment, primer 2 73% (p=0.24); primer 1 under-referred (93% of misalignments), primers 2 and 3 over-referred (88%, 100%; p<0.001). Burns: primer 1 55% vs 85% (p=0.041).
evidence.quote: The nature of the errors varied significantly by primer with primer 1 significantly more likely to under-refer (93% of its misalignments), while primers 2 and 3 tended toward over-referral (88% and 100% of misalignments, respectively; p < 0.001).

evidence.title: Evaluating large language models as clinical laboratory test recommenders in primary and emergency care: a crucial step in clinical decision making
evidence.outcome: Self-consistency of GPT-4o recommendations across repeated prompts versus expert order consistency
evidence.effect: GPT-4o exhibited high self-consistency across repeated prompts, surpassing the consistency observed among individual expert orders in the earliest round of consensus.
evidence.quote: We found that GPT-4o exhibited high self-consistency across repeated prompts, surpassing the consistency observed among individual expert orders in the earliest round of consensus.

evidence.title: From Guidelines to Real-Time Conversation: Expert-Validated Retrieval-Augmented and Fine-Tuned GPT-4 for Hepatitis C Management
evidence.venue: Liver international : official journal of the International Association for the Study of the Liver
evidence.outcome: Effect of temperature/top-p settings and repeated runs on answer similarity to expert answers
evidence.effect: Optimal at temperature 0-0.8 and top-p 0-0.5; all models declined dramatically at temperature >=1.4 and top-p >=0.7; RAG-Top10 most robust.
evidence.quote: All models exhibit a dramatic performance decline with temperature ≥ 1.4 and Top‐ p ≥ 0.7, confirming that higher values introduce excessive variability in responses.
evidence.sample_unit: queries (15 open-ended questions and 25 simulated clinical scenarios)

evidence.title: Enhancing the CAD-RADS™ 2.0 Category Assignment Performance of ChatGPT and DeepSeek Through "Few-shot" Prompting
evidence.outcome: Reproducibility of few-shot classifications across repeated runs on 50 reports
evidence.effect: Kappa 0.957 (0.900, 1.000) for ChatGPT and 0.873 (0.779, 0.967) for DeepSeek between repeated assignments.
evidence.quote: Reproducibility analysis yielded kappa values of 0.957 (0.900, 1.000) ( P <0.001) for ChatGPT and 0.873 [0.779, 0.967] ( P <0.001) for DeepSeek, indicating almost perfect and strong agreement between repeated assignments, respectively, with no significant difference between the models ( P =0.125).

evidence.title: AI meets sleep surgery: assessing drug-induced sleep endoscopy interpretation with a large language model
evidence.outcome: Reproducibility of LLM treatment recommendations across independent runs
evidence.effect: Model-generated treatment recommendations were highly reproducible between independent runs.
evidence.quote: Model-generated treatment recommendations were safe, consistent with accepted clinical practice, and highly reproducible between independent runs.

evidence.title: Accounting for inconclusive results and repeated testing: A framework for evaluating wearable electrocardiogram diagnostic performance with application to Apple Watch and artificial intelligence-enhanced interpretation
evidence.outcome: output reproducibility
evidence.effect: Repeatability across attempts was substantial for Apple Watch (kappa 0.77) and near-perfect for AI (0.96).
evidence.quote: Repeatability was substantial for Apple Watch (kappa 0.77) and near-perfect for AI (0.96).

evidence.title: Automated chain-of-thought evaluation framework for large language model-generated emergency department documentation: a simulation-based study
evidence.outcome: Reproducibility of LLM evaluator outputs across repeated runs (ICC)
evidence.effect: High reproducibility confirmed (ICC >0.919), with Claude-3.5 most consistent (ICC, 0.997-0.998).
evidence.quote: High reproducibility was confirmed (ICC >0.919), with Claude-3.5 achieving the most consistent results (ICC, 0.997-0.998).

evidence.title: Baseline Evaluation of Claude Opus 4 for Diabetes Management: A Preliminary Assessment and Lessons for Implementation
evidence.outcome: Reproducibility of LLM answers across repeated runs on diabetes questions
evidence.effect: High response reproducibility (96.7%) across repeated runs on 30 diabetes questions, with 80% accuracy.
evidence.quote: Claude Opus 4 achieved 80% accuracy in general diabetes knowledge, with high response reproducibility (96.7%), indicating baseline rather than clinically adequate performance.

evidence.title: Can large language models aid pre-surgical epileptogenic zone localization? A multi-source text analysis performance study in drug-resistant epilepsy
evidence.outcome: Test-retest reliability of LLM predictions across repeated runs
evidence.effect: Predictions exhibited excellent test-retest reliability (ICC = 0.951)
evidence.quote: Predictions exhibited excellent test-retest reliability (ICC = 0.951), and higher SEEG stratification scores were assigned to patients who underwent invasive monitoring (p < 0.001).

evidence.title: Evaluating Retrieval-Augmented Generation-Large Language Models for Infective Endocarditis Prophylaxis: Clinical Accuracy and Efficiency
evidence.outcome: Response consistency across five repeated runs, with and without preprompt
evidence.effect: Consistency ranged 78.6-96.4%; Claude 3.7 Sonnet highest at 96.4% without preprompt; preprompting increased consistency for some models and decreased it for Gemini 1.5 Pro, Llama 3.3 70b, Grok 3 beta.
evidence.quote: Consistency increased for Claude 3.5 Sonnet, DeepSeek Reasoner, and GPT-o3-mini, but decreased for Gemini 1.5 Pro, Llama 3.3 70b, and Grok 3 beta.
evidence.sample_unit: questions (true/false, 5 runs per model); plus 10 dental students in pilot

evidence.title: Comparative Performance of ChatGPT-4o, Grok-3, and Claude 3.7 Sonnet in Differentiating Cerebellopontine Angle Schwannomas and Meningiomas: A Pilot Study of Visual Versus Text-Based Diagnostic Prompting
evidence.venue: Journal of imaging informatics in medicine
evidence.outcome: LLM accuracy under varied input quality (expert vs resident structured features vs raw images)
evidence.effect: Accuracy fell from 86.8-94.3% (expert features) to 71.7-73.6% (resident features) to 18.9-52.8% (raw images), showing brittleness to input variation.
evidence.quote: Performance degrades moderately with resident-derived features and dramatically with raw image input, highlighting the critical importance of structured prompting for clinical LLM applications.

evidence.title: Out of the Laboratory and Into the Clinic: Out-of-Domain Validation of Machine Learning Models for Velopharyngeal Dysfunction Detection
evidence.outcome: Model performance under real-world recording variation versus standardized test set
evidence.effect: Whisper/SVM reached 100% accuracy in-domain; out-of-domain deep learning models failed to generalize; MFCC/SVM best at 64.1% accuracy, macro F1 0.61.
evidence.quote: Cross-domain generalization testing on the out-of-domain dataset demonstrated severe performance degradation.

evidence.title: Bridging the analog divide: a comparison of printed X-ray films and digital images when using computer-aided detection software for tuberculosis screening
evidence.outcome: AUC and specificity when input format changes from DICOM to photographed film JPEG
evidence.effect: AUC did not differ significantly (0.94 vs 0.92, p = 0.190), but specificity was significantly lower with JPEG (e.g., 95.2% vs 92.1%, p < 0.001) and abnormality scores were higher.
evidence.quote: There is no significant difference in the AUC for the Genki CAD software when processing either DICOM or JPEG files (0.94 vs 0.92, p = 0.190).

evidence.title: Multi-Evidence Clinical Reasoning With Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Emergency Triage: Retrospective Evaluation Study
evidence.outcome: Output reproducibility across repeated runs and across LLM backends
evidence.effect: Five independent runs gave QWK SD 0.0021 for MECR-RAG; advantage robust to run-to-run variability; single-run gains on Claude 3.7 (0.840 to 0.890) and GPT-4o (0.778 to 0.890).
evidence.quote: Similar effect sizes were observed when analyses were repeated using single median‑run prediction sets, indicating that MECR‑RAG’s advantage was robust to run‑to‑run variability.

evidence.title: Diagnostic Performance of ChatGPT-5 for Detecting Pediatric Pneumothorax on Chest Radiographs: A Multi-Prompt Evaluation
evidence.outcome: Diagnostic performance and reproducibility across three prompt formulations
evidence.effect: Accuracy 0.77-0.79 and specificity 0.96-0.98 across all prompts with stable reproducibility; no significant differences among prompting strategies.
evidence.quote: No significant differences were observed among prompting strategies.

evidence.title: Prospective quantitative analysis of hyperparameter and input optimization in GPT-5: comparative contribution to radiologist performance in abdominal radiology
evidence.outcome: GPT-5 performance across input formats, temperature/top-p settings, and repeat-run reproducibility
evidence.effect: Accuracy 12% image-only vs 58% with text; 53% to 73% across temperatures; Round 2 agreement kappa 0.882 for diagnosis, no significant difference (P=0.41). Temperature 2 outputs were unevaluable.
evidence.quote: Agreement between GPT-5 responses generated with the optimal settings at baseline and in the Round 2 evaluation was high, with Cohen’s κ: 0.882 (95% CI: 0.80–0.96) for the most likely diagnosis and κ: 0.816 for differential diagnosis performance, indicating strong agreement.

evidence.title: Digitally Assisted Clinical Decision-Making in Traditional Chinese Medicine: Comparative Study of 5 Large Language Models
evidence.outcome: Output reproducibility across repeated runs and model consistency

evidence.title: Complete Blood Count and Monocyte Distribution Width-Based Machine Learning Algorithms for Sepsis Detection: Multicentric Development and External Validation Study

evidence.title: Evaluating performance of large language models for atrial fibrillation management using different prompting strategies and languages
evidence.outcome: LLM classification reliability and consistency across prompting strategies, languages, and repeated runs
evidence.effect: Fleiss kappa 0.449 to 0.763 across LLM-prompt combinations (moderate to substantial); best consistency 60.3% (Claude 3.5 with P-COT); no significant English vs Chinese differences in most combinations.

evidence.title: Developing artificial intelligence tools for institutional review board pre-review: A pilot study on ChatGPT's accuracy and reproducibility
evidence.outcome: Reproducibility of extraction across 10 repeated runs; structured custom prompts vs standard prompts

evidence.title: Can AI Outperform Human Aspirants? Evaluating 3 ChatGPT Models on the Spanish FIR and BIR Specialized Health Examinations

evidence.quote: The reproducibility analysis showed GPT-o1's tendency to correct previous mistakes on retesting, while GPT-4o and GPT-4o Mini more consistently repeated initial answers.

evidence.title: A Multimodal Large Language Model as an End-to-End Classifier of Thyroid Nodule Malignancy Risk: Usability Study
evidence.outcome: Effect of prompt engineering and image labeling on accuracy and run-to-run consistency of TI-RADS outputs

evidence.title: Assessing the Impact of the Quality of Textual Data on Feature Representation and Machine Learning Models: Quantitative Study Using Large Language Models

evidence.title: Effects of Image Degradation on Deep Neural Network Classification of Scaphoid Fracture Radiographs: Comparison Study of Different Noise Types
evidence.outcome: Classifier accuracy under perturbed inputs (blur, noise, JPEG, CLAHE, resizing, screenshots) versus clean images

evidence.title: Automated Tumor and Node Staging from Esophageal Cancer Endoscopic Ultrasound Reports: A Benchmark of Advanced Reasoning Models with Prompt Engineering and Cross-Lingual Evaluation

evidence.title: Measuring the Accuracy and Reproducibility of DeepSeek R1, Claude 3.5 Sonnet, and GPT-4.1 on Complex Clinical Scenarios

evidence.title: Mapping the susceptibility of large language models to medical misinformation across clinical notes and social media: a cross-sectional benchmarking analysis

evidence.quote: Eight of ten fallacy framings significantly reduced or did not change that rate, led by appeal to popularity (susceptibility 11·9%; difference of -19·8 percentage points; p<0·0001); only the slippery-slope prompt (33·9%; difference of 2·2 percentage points; p<0·0001) and the appeal-to-authority prompt (34·6%; difference of 2·9 percentage points; p<0·0001) increased it.

evidence.title: Performance of Large Language Models Under Input Variability in Health Care Applications: Dataset Development and Experimental Evaluation

evidence.title: Benchmark evaluation of large language models for clinical decision support in headache management

evidence.title: An automatic consult reply system for therapeutic plasma exchange using retrieval-augmented generation

evidence.title: DeepSeek vs ChatGPT vs Claude: benchmarking large language models for clinical diagnosis using a novel ICD-10-CM-based evaluation framework

evidence.title: Performance of large language models in urological decision support: a guideline-based comparative evaluation in urolithiasis

evidence.title: Case-matched retrieval improves textual alignment of LLM-generated radiology impressions

evidence.title: INFORMER-Interpretability-Founded Monitoring of Medical Image Deep Learning Models: Application to Chest X-ray Pathologies

evidence.title: A deep-learning model for intracranial aneurysm detection on CT angiography images in China: a stepwise, multicentre, early-stage clinical validation study

evidence.title: Development and Validation of a Large Language Model-Based System for Medical History-Taking Training: Prospective Multicase Study on Evaluation Stability, Human-AI Consistency, and Transparency

evidence.outcome: Cross-modal alignment under adversarial clinical-radiological mismatch cases

evidence.quote: In comprehensive diagnostic analysis tasks (Q29-Q30), models exhibited "textual masking," aligning visual findings with text cues rather than imaging evidence.

evidence.quote: The intra-examiner reliability of the AI was exceptionally high (κ = 0.987).

evidence.title: Embedding-Based Evaluation and Benchmarking Framework for Optimizing LLM Post-Processing of Medical Transcriptions from a Local Whisper System
evidence.venue: Studies in health technology and informatics

evidence.quote: Stability analysis showed high consistency across repeated runs, with cosine similarities typically exceeding 0.90, while higher sampling temperatures reduced semantic similarity.

evidence.title: Large Language Models in Multidisciplinary Decision-Making for Hepatopancreatobiliary Oncology: Retrospective Comparative Feasibility Study
evidence.outcome: Reproducibility of LLM treatment recommendations across 4 repeated identical queries
evidence.effect: Stability differed significantly across models (P=.01). Gemini 3 Pro discordance 12.8% (Fleiss κ=0.737); GPT-4o discordance 30.2% (Fleiss κ=0.430). Complete discordance in 17 of 107 (15.9%) cases.

evidence.title: Concordance between GPT-4 and a multidisciplinary tumor board in pancreatic cancer: A prospective pilot study
