evidence.quote: In some instances, responses were brief and lacked contextual detail, whereas in other seemingly similar cases, they were substantially more comprehensive (Fig. 3 C/D).

evidence.title: RadCoT: a Radiological Chain-of-Thought framework for enhanced error detection in radiology reports
evidence.outcome: LLM error-detection F1 under standard prompting versus structured RadCoT prompting across seven models
evidence.effect: Mean micro-averaged F1 rose from 0.77 ± 0.06 (standard) to 0.85 ± 0.06 (RadCoT; p = 0.003); interpretation errors improved from 0.57 to 0.75.
evidence.quote: RadCoT significantly improved the mean micro-averaged F1 across all models from 0.77 ± 0.06 (standard) to 0.85 ± 0.06 (RadCoT; p = 0.003).

evidence.title: On the Robustness of Answer Formats in Medical Reasoning Models
evidence.outcome: Answer-format robustness (correctness across multiple-choice, open-ended, ranked list formats) across 15 models
evidence.effect: Substantial variation in format robustness across 15 models (35-100%); reinforcement fine-tuning often shows higher cross-format brittleness than supervised fine-tuning.
evidence.quote: Across 15 proprietary and open-weight models, we observe substantial variation in format robustness (35-100%).

evidence.title: From Conversation to Query Execution: Benchmarking User and Tool Interactions for EHR Database Agents
evidence.outcome: Consistency of agent success across five repeated trials (Pass^5 vs Pass@5)
evidence.effect: Best agents reach Pass@5 over 90% on IncreQA and 60-70% on AdaptQA, but Pass^5 is substantially lower, with gaps of up to about 60%.
evidence.quote: Experiments with state-of-the-art LLMs (e.g., o4-mini and Gemini-2.5-Flash) over five i.i.d. trials show that while the best-performing agents achieve Pass@5 of over 90% (at least one of five trials) on IncreQA and 60-70% on AdaptQA, their Pass^5 (consistent success across all five trials) is substantially lower, with gaps of up to about 60%.
evidence.sample_unit: benchmark conversations (five i.i.d. trials per agent)

evidence.title: Radiology's Last Exam (RadLE): Benchmarking Frontier Multimodal AI Against Human Experts and a Taxonomy of Visual Reasoning Errors in Radiology
evidence.outcome: Reproducibility of model diagnoses across three independent runs
evidence.effect: Reliability substantial for GPT-5 and o3, moderate for Gemini 2.5 Pro and Grok-4, and poor for Claude Opus 4.1.
evidence.quote: Reliability was substantial for GPT-5 and o3, moderate for Gemini 2.5 Pro and Grok-4, and poor for Claude Opus 4.1.

evidence.title: Shallow Robustness, Deep Vulnerabilities: Multi-Turn Evaluation of Medical LLMs
evidence.outcome: LLM accuracy under misleading context and challenged answers across multi-turn medical QA
evidence.effect: Accuracy dropped from 91.2% to as low as 13.5% for Claude Sonnet 4 in multi-turn settings. Models did reasonably well under shallow perturbations. Indirect, context-based interventions were often more harmful than direct suggestions.
evidence.quote: Using controlled interventions on the MedQA dataset, we evaluate five state-of-the-art LLMs and find that while models perform reasonably well under shallow perturbations, they exhibit severe vulnerabilities in multi-turn settings, with accuracy dropping from 91.2% to as low as 13.5% for Claude Sonnet 4.

evidence.title: GAPS: A Clinically Grounded, Automated Benchmark for Evaluating AI Clinicians
evidence.outcome: Model robustness to adversarial perturbations on the P-axis of the GAPS benchmark
evidence.effect: Models were reported as highly vulnerable to adversarial perturbations (P-axis); performance also degraded sharply with reasoning depth (G-axis). No numeric effect sizes were given in the abstract.
evidence.quote: Evaluating state-of-the-art models on the benchmark revealed key failure modes: performance degrades sharply with increased reasoning depth (G-axis), models struggle with answer completeness (A-axis), and they are highly vulnerable to adversarial perturbations (P-axis) as well as certain safety issues (S-axis).

evidence.title: Stable Prediction of Adverse Events in Medical Time-Series Data
evidence.outcome: Accuracy and temporal stability of per-patient risk trajectories across six early event prediction tasks
evidence.effect: Existing methods, especially LLMs, struggle to jointly optimize accuracy and stability, with notably poor recall at high-precision operating points.
evidence.quote: Across tasks, existing methods, especially LLMs, struggle to jointly optimize accuracy and stability, with notably poor recall at high-precision operating points.

evidence.title: TCM-5CEval: Extended Deep Evaluation Benchmark for LLM's Comprehensive Clinical Research Competence in Traditional Chinese Medicine
evidence.outcome: LLM accuracy under permuted answer-option order in TCM benchmark questions
evidence.effect: All 15 evaluated models, including top scorers, showed substantial performance degradation when option ordering was varied, indicating positional bias and fragile inference. No numbers given in the abstract.
evidence.quote: All evaluated models, including the highest-scoring ones, displayed a substantial performance degradation when faced with varied question option ordering, indicating a pervasive sensitivity to positional bias and a lack of robust understanding.

evidence.title: Script Gap: Evaluating LLM Triage on Indian Languages in Native vs Romanized Scripts in a Real World Setting
evidence.outcome: LLM triage robustness to real-world orthographic input variation (romanization)
evidence.effect: Performance degrades consistently on romanized input, with gaps of up to 24 points across languages and models.
evidence.quote: Our results reveal consistent degradation in performance for romanized messages, with gap reaching up to 24 points across languages and models.
languages: Indian languages (five, not named in abstract)

evidence.title: DL$^3$M: A Vision-to-Language Framework for Expert-Level Medical Reasoning through Deep Learning and Large Language Models
evidence.outcome: Stability of LLM clinical reasoning when prompts vary
evidence.effect: None of the 32 LLMs reached human-level stability; even the best LLMs changed their reasoning when prompts varied.
evidence.quote: Even the best LLMs change their reasoning when prompts vary.

evidence.title: Measuring Stability Beyond Accuracy in Small Open-Source Medical Large Language Models for Pediatric Endocrinology
evidence.outcome: Output divergence under semantically negligible prompt perturbations and system-level differences such as CUDA builds
evidence.effect: Small, semantically negligible prompt perturbations led to divergent outputs; CUDA build differences produced statistically significant shifts in model output despite stable accuracy.
evidence.quote: This work demonstrates that small, semantically negligible prompt perturbations lead to divergent outputs, raising concerns about reproducibility of LLM-based evaluations and highlights the output variability under different stochastic regimes, emphasizing the need of a broader diagnostic framework to understand potential pitfalls in real-world clinical decision support scenarios.

evidence.title: Faithfulness vs. Safety: Evaluating LLM Behavior Under Counterfactual Medical Evidence
evidence.outcome: LLM responses to counterfactual, dangerous or implausible medical evidence supplied as context
evidence.effect: Models overwhelmingly accepted counterfactual evidence at face value, even when dangerous or implausible, rather than rejecting it. Exact rates not given in the abstract.
evidence.quote: Our evaluation across multiple frontier LLMs on MedCounterFact reveals that in the presence of counterfactual evidence, existing models overwhelmingly accept such "evidence" at face value even when it is dangerous or implausible, and provide confident and uncaveated answers.

evidence.title: The Paradox of Robustness: Decoupling Rule-Based Logic from Affective Noise in High-Stakes Decision-Making
evidence.outcome: Decision shift under emotional framing perturbations of rule-bound prompts across eight LLMs
evidence.effect: Negligible effect size (Cohen's h = 0.003) versus human biases (h in [0.3, 0.8]); immigration extension +0.8 percentage point shift within +/-3 pp ROPE; adversarial narrative pilot found no meaningful decision shift.
evidence.quote: we find a negligible effect size (Cohen's h = 0.003) compared to the substantial biases observed in analogous human contexts (h in [0.3, 0.8]), approximately two orders of magnitude smaller.
evidence.sample_unit: unique prompts (9 base scenarios x 18 condition variants)

evidence.title: PSF-Med: Measuring and Explaining Paraphrase Sensitivity in Medical Vision Language Models
evidence.outcome: Answer flip rate under meaning-preserving paraphrases of chest X-ray questions across nine VLMs
evidence.effect: Flip rates from 3% to 37% across nine VLMs; some low-flip models stay consistent even with image removed, suggesting reliance on language priors.
evidence.quote: Across nine VLMs, including general-purpose models, we find flip rates from 3% to 37%.

evidence.title: Agentic retrieval-augmented reasoning reshapes collective reliability under model variability in radiology question answering
evidence.outcome: Correctness and agreement across heterogeneous models on radiology questions
evidence.effect: High agreement did not guarantee correctness; consensus strength and robust correctness correlated (rho=0.88 zero-shot; 0.87 agentic).
evidence.quote: Consensus strength and robust correctness remained correlated under both strategies (\r{ho}=0.88 for zero-shot; \r{ho}=0.87 for agentic), although high agreement did not guarantee correctness.

evidence.title: ThReadMed-QA: A Multi-Turn Medical Dialogue Benchmark from Real Patient Questions
evidence.outcome: Multi-turn consistency and error propagation across conversation turns
evidence.effect: Wrong-answer rates roughly tripled by turn 2; a single wrong turn raised the probability of a subsequent wrong turn by 1.9-6.1x; nearly one in three Claude Haiku conversations swung between fully correct and completely wrong.
evidence.quote: EPR shows that a single wrong turn raises the probability of a subsequent wrong turn by 1.9-6.1x across all models.

evidence.title: PathGLS: Evaluating Pathology Vision-Language Models without Ground Truth through Multi-Dimensional Consistency
evidence.outcome: Pathology VLM output stability under adversarial visual-semantic perturbations
evidence.effect: PathGLS Stability dimension measures output variance under adversarial perturbations; PathGLS sensitivity dropped 40.2% for hallucinated reports versus 2.1% for BERTScore.
evidence.quote: Specifically, on the Quilt-1M dataset, PathGLS reveals a steep sensitivity drop of 40.2% for hallucinated reports compared to only 2.1% for BERTScore.

evidence.title: CoDA: Exploring Chain-of-Distribution Attacks and Post-Hoc Token-Space Repair for Medical Vision-Language Models
evidence.outcome: Zero-shot MVLM performance under clinically plausible pipeline shifts (acquisition, reconstruction, display, delivery) on MRI, chest X-ray, CT
evidence.effect: CoDA substantially degrades zero-shot performance of CLIP-style MVLMs; chained compositions were consistently more damaging than any single stage. Numbers not reported in the abstract.
evidence.quote: Across brain MRI, chest X-ray, and abdominal CT, CoDA substantially degrades the zero-shot performance of CLIP-style MVLMs, with chained compositions consistently more damaging than any single stage.

evidence.title: TimeTox: An LLM-Based Pipeline for Automated Extraction of Time Toxicity from Clinical Trial Protocols
evidence.outcome: Reproducibility of LLM time toxicity extraction across 3 repeated runs on real-world protocols
evidence.effect: Vanilla pipeline: 95.3% clinically acceptable (IQR ≤ 3 days) across 3 runs on 644 protocols; 82.0% perfect stability (IQR = 0), so about 18% of protocols showed run-to-run variation.
evidence.quote: However, on real-world protocols, the vanilla pipeline showed superior reproducibility: 95.3% clinically acceptable accuracy (IQR $\leq$ 3 days) across 3 runs on 644 protocols, with 82.0% perfect stability (IQR = 0).
evidence.sample_unit: real-world oncology protocols (plus 20 synthetic schedules, 240 comparisons)

evidence.title: MedMT-Bench: Can LLMs Memorize and Understand Long Multi-Turn Conversations in Medical Scenarios?
evidence.outcome: Accuracy on long multi-turn medical instruction following, including interference robustness and safety defense
evidence.effect: All 17 frontier models scored below 60.00% overall accuracy; the best model reached 59.75%.
evidence.quote: We test 17 frontier models, all of which underperform on MedMT-Bench (overall accuracy below 60.00\%), with the best model reaching 59.75\%.

evidence.title: When Chain-of-Thought Backfires: Evaluating Prompt Sensitivity in Medical Language Models
evidence.outcome: Prediction stability and accuracy under answer-option shuffling, few-shot, CoT, and context truncation perturbations
evidence.effect: Shuffling options changed predictions 59.1% of the time, accuracy dropping up to 27.4 points; few-shot lowered performance 11.9% and raised position bias from 0.14 to 0.47; CoT lowered accuracy 5.7%.
evidence.quote: Shuffling answer options causes the model to change predictions 59.1% of the time, with accuracy dropping up to 27.4 percentage points.

evidence.title: Automating Clinical Information Retrieval from Finnish Electronic Health Records Using Large Language Models
evidence.outcome: Consistency of LLM answers across semantically equivalent question variants
evidence.effect: Llama-3.1-70B had 97.3% consistency, but equivalent questions occasionally gave discordant responses; one correct and one clinically significant error in 0.96% of cases.
evidence.quote: semantically equivalent questions occasionally yielded discordant responses, including instances where one formulation was correct and the other contained a clinically significant error (0.96% of cases).

evidence.title: Beyond Idealized Patients: Evaluating LLMs under Challenging Patient Behaviors in Medical Consultations
evidence.outcome: LLM response safety to contradictory, inaccurate, self-diagnosing, or care-resistant patient utterances
evidence.effect: Models performed well overall but showed consistent behavior-specific failure patterns, with particular difficulty on contradictory or medically implausible patient information.
evidence.quote: While models perform well overall, we identify consistent, behavior-specific failure patterns, with particular difficulty in handling contradictory or medically implausible patient information.

evidence.title: Benchmarking Multi-turn Medical Diagnosis: Hold, Lure, and Self-Correction
evidence.outcome: LLM diagnostic behavior when clinical evidence is released incrementally across turns rather than in a single turn
evidence.effect: Over 55% of answers were committed within the first two turns. Salient evidence such as lab results triggered premature answering even when models were told to wait. Premature commitment caused accuracy drops of up to 23.3%.
evidence.quote: We translate these findings into clinically actionable guidance: deferring the diagnostic question to later turns reduces premature answering and improves accuracy at the first point of commitment by up to 62.6%, while reserving salient clinical evidence for later turns prevents a catastrophic accuracy drop of up to 23.3% caused by premature commitment.

evidence.title: This Treatment Works, Right? Evaluating LLM Sensitivity to Patient Question Framing in Medical QA
evidence.outcome: Response consistency under paraphrased or reframed medical questions with identical evidence
evidence.effect: Opposite-framing query pairs were significantly more likely to produce contradictory conclusions across eight LLMs; inconsistency increased with sustained persuasion in multi-turn conversations.
evidence.quote: Our findings show that positively- and negatively-framed pairs are significantly more likely to produce contradictory conclusions than same-framing pairs.

evidence.title: MedDialBench: Benchmarking LLM Diagnostic Robustness under Parametric Adversarial Patient Behaviors
evidence.outcome: LLM diagnostic accuracy under perturbed patient inputs (fabricated or withheld information)
evidence.effect: Fabricating symptoms produced 1.7-3.4x larger accuracy drops than withholding information. Fabricating was significant across all five models (McNemar p<0.05). Worst-case drops ranged from 38.8 to 54.1 percentage points.
evidence.quote: we find a fundamental asymmetry: information pollution (fabricating symptoms) produces 1.7-3.4x larger accuracy drops than information deficit (withholding information), and fabricating is the only configuration achieving statistical significance across all five models (McNemar p < 0.05).
evidence.sample_unit: dialogues (85 cases x 17 configurations x 5 models)

evidence.title: To Adapt or not to Adapt, Rethinking the Value of Medical Knowledge-Aware Large Language Models
evidence.outcome: Model robustness to perturbed questions, instruction following, and strict output formatting
evidence.effect: Both general and clinical models showed substantial limitations in instruction following and strict output formatting; clinical models did not consistently beat general models even under the perturbation benchmark. No numbers in abstract.
evidence.quote: We further find that both general and clinical models exhibit substantial limitations in instruction following and strict output formatting.
evidence.sample_unit: multiple-choice clinical questions (English and Spanish benchmark subsets)

evidence.title: Evaluating Small Open LLMs for Medical Question Answering: A Practical Framework
evidence.outcome: Output reproducibility across 10 repeated runs per question at low temperature
evidence.effect: Self-agreement across runs reaches at most 0.20 despite T=0.2, while 87-97% of all outputs per model are unique.
evidence.quote: Evaluating three models (Llama 3.1 8B, Gemma 3 12B, MedGemma 1.5 4B) on 50 MedQuAD questions (N=1,500 total responses) reveals that despite low-temperature generation (T=0.2), self-agreement across runs reaches at most 0.20, while 87-97% of all outputs per model are unique -- a safety gap that single-pass benchmarks entirely miss.
evidence.sample_unit: responses (50 MedQuAD questions x 10 runs x 3 models)

evidence.title: How Robust Are Large Language Models for Clinical Numeracy? An Empirical Study on Numerical Reasoning Abilities in Clinical Contexts
evidence.outcome: LLM numeracy accuracy across semantically equivalent clinical note formats
evidence.effect: Performance dropped under note-style variation, indicating format sensitivity. Value retrieval was mostly above 85% accuracy; relational comparison and aggregation were weak, with some models below 15%.
evidence.quote: Fine-tuning on medical data can reduce numeracy relative to base models by over 30%, and performance drops under note-style variation indicate LLM sensitivity to format.

evidence.title: Consistency of AI-Generated Exercise Prescriptions: A Repeated Generation Study Using a Large Language Model
evidence.outcome: Reproducibility of LLM exercise prescriptions across repeated identical generations (semantic, structural, safety consistency)
evidence.effect: Mean cosine similarity 0.879-0.939; frequency consistent, but intensity varied, with 10-25% of resistance training intensity expressions unclassifiable; safety sentence counts varied significantly across scenarios (H=86.18, p<0.001).
evidence.quote: LLM-generated exercise prescriptions demonstrated high semantic consistency but showed variability in key quantitative components.
evidence.sample_unit: LLM-generated exercise prescriptions (20 per scenario, 6 scenarios)

evidence.title: Green Shielding: A User-Centric Approach Towards Trustworthy AI
evidence.outcome: LLM diagnostic output sensitivity to realistic non-adversarial input variation
evidence.effect: Benign input variation shifted outputs, tracing Pareto-like tradeoffs across multiple frontier LLMs. Neutralization reduced coverage of highly likely and safety-critical conditions.
evidence.quote: Across multiple frontier LLMs, these shifts trace out Pareto-like tradeoffs.

evidence.title: CLEAR: Revealing How Noise and Ambiguity Degrade Reliability in LLMs for Medicine
evidence.outcome: LLM reliability under perturbed answer-option count, abstention option presence, and semantic framing
evidence.effect: Perturbing the decision space degraded reliability. Adding an IDK option increased incorrect answer selections. No numeric results are given in the abstract.
evidence.quote: Notably, just including IDK in the answer space increases incorrect answer selections.
evidence.sample_unit: LLMs evaluated across three medical benchmarks

evidence.title: Compared to What? Baselines and Metrics for Counterfactual Prompting
evidence.outcome: Prediction flips on medical QA under meaning-preserving paraphrase of inputs
evidence.effect: Paraphrasing inputs alone induced prediction flip rates of 14.1% on MedQA, similar to the 14.9% from changing patient gender.
evidence.quote: However, this is statistically indistinguishable from the flip rates induced by simply paraphrasing inputs (14.1%).

evidence.title: Can We Trust LLMs for Mental Health Screening? Consistency, ASR Robustness, and Evidence Faithfulness
evidence.outcome: Intra-model score consistency across repeated runs and under ASR transcription noise
evidence.effect: Phi-4 and Gemma-2-9B ICC > 0.89 with minimal degradation under ASR; Llama-3.1-8B ICC dropped from 0.82 to 0.36 at 10% WER.
evidence.quote: Llama-3.1-8B shows ASR-fragile consistency, with ICC dropping from 0.82 to 0.36 at 10% WER

evidence.title: MedMeta: A Benchmark for LLMs in Synthesizing Meta-Analysis Conclusion from Medical Studies
evidence.outcome: Whether models identify and reject negated evidence in stress tests
evidence.effect: All models, regardless of architecture, failed to identify and reject negated evidence, described as a critical vulnerability in current RAG systems.
evidence.quote: Furthermore, stress tests show that all models, regardless of architecture, fail to identify and reject negated evidence, highlighting a critical vulnerability in current RAG systems.

evidence.title: When AI Tells You What You Want to Hear: Sycophantic Behavior of Large Language Models in Dementia Care Settings
evidence.outcome: Response quality change across prompts with increasing confirmatory and authority framing in dementia care
evidence.effect: All four LLMs showed negative Spearman correlations between prompt level and quality (rho -0.543 to -0.734, all p<0.01); Mistral Large mean score fell from 6.0/7 at P1 to 0.2/7 at P5.
evidence.quote: All models showed significant negative Spearman correlations between prompt level and response quality (rho ranging from -0.543 to -0.734, all p < 0.01).

evidence.title: What Does the AI Doctor Value? Auditing Pluralism in the Clinical Ethics of Language Models
evidence.outcome: Decision consistency across repeated sampling and semantic variations of dilemma prompts
evidence.effect: Individual model decisions were near-deterministic across repeated sampling and semantic variations, so no brittleness or nondeterminism. The consistency failed to reproduce the physician panel's distributional pluralism.
evidence.quote: However, individual model decisions are near-deterministic across repeated sampling and semantic variations, failing to reproduce the distributional pluralism of the physician panel.

evidence.title: When Correct Beliefs Collapse: Epistemic Resilience of LLMs under Clinical Pressure
evidence.outcome: Belief stability of correct diagnoses under escalating multi-turn pressure across nine LLMs
evidence.effect: High initial diagnostic capability did not imply high belief stability, yielding large knowledge-robustness gaps for several LLMs.
evidence.quote: Across nine frontier large language models (LLMs), we find a clear dissociation between medical knowledge and robustness: high initial diagnostic capability does not imply high belief stability, yielding large knowledge-robustness gaps for several LLMs.

evidence.title: Same Patient, Different Words, Different Diagnosis? Evaluating Semantic Stability in Clinical LLMs
evidence.outcome: Robustness of general-purpose vs medical LLMs to meaning-preserving prompt reformulations on DiagnosisQA and MedQA
evidence.effect: Robustness differences between domain-specific and general-purpose models were mixed and model-dependent; some DS models were among the most robust, and strong GP baselines stayed competitive. Sensitivity to rephrasing is described as a risk.
evidence.quote: Our results demonstrate that robustness differences between domain-specific (DS) models are mixed and highly model-dependent, i.e., domain specialization does not consistently improve or reduce robustness to meaning-preserving prompt reformulations.

evidence.title: Can I Take Another Dose? Evaluating LLM Decision-Making Under Temporal Uncertainty in OTC Dosing QA
evidence.outcome: Consistency of LLM dosing answers across repeated runs
evidence.effect: Stable or confident-looking responses can still violate dosing constraints; consistency assessed across repeated runs, with 1,620 responses evaluated.
evidence.quote: Our results show that models frequently struggle with rolling-window reasoning and ambiguity-sensitive cases and that stable or confident-looking responses can still violate dosing constraints.
evidence.sample_unit: model responses (81 scenarios, 4 LLMs, repeated runs)

evidence.title: Measuring the sensitivity of LLM-based structured extraction to prompt, model, and schema choices in clinical discharge summaries
evidence.outcome: Output agreement across prompt paraphrases and model choices in structured extraction
evidence.effect: Median cross-prompt kappa 0.69 and 0.68 on three-way flags; model change reassigns dominant admission tag on close to half of notes, prompt phrasing on roughly one in eight.
evidence.quote: On the multi-class admission categorization, changing the model reassigns the dominant tag on close to half of all notes while changing the prompt phrasing reassigns it on roughly one in eight, and the larger model places far less mass on residual catch-all categories (44% to 26%).

evidence.title: When Large Language Models Fail in Healthcare: Evaluating Sensitivity to Prompt Variations
evidence.outcome: LLM robustness to lexical, syntactic, and adversarial prompt perturbations on MedMCQA
evidence.effect: Models resilient to simple lexical substitutions or paraphrasing but break down under syntactic reordering or misleading contextual cues; fragility across general-purpose and medical LLMs. No numbers in abstract.
evidence.quote: While models tend to show resilience to simple lexical substitutions or paraphrasing, they often break down under syntactic reordering or misleading contextual cues.

evidence.title: Stress-testing medical large language models reveals latent safety pathology beyond benchmark accuracy
evidence.outcome: LLM performance under narrative perturbation probes versus clean baseline
evidence.effect: All models performed uniformly well at baseline; under narrative stress performance diverged sharply, with two stress-response phenotypes. Quantized models showed pseudonormalization (low flip rates hiding functional collapse).
evidence.quote: Under realistic narrative stress, performance diverged sharply, revealing two distinct stress-response phenotypes.

evidence.title: Measuring Epistemic Resilience of LLMs Under Misleading Medical Context
evidence.outcome: LLM accuracy and attack success under injected misleading context versus original questions
evidence.effect: Mean accuracy fell from 71.1% on original questions to 38.0% under focused misleading context, with 51.5% attack success across 11 model configurations.
evidence.quote: Across 11 model configurations, mean accuracy falls from 71.1% on original questions to 38.0% under focused misleading context, with 51.5% attack success.

evidence.title: When Prompts Mislead: Textual Dominance and Diagnostic Bias in MLLMs
evidence.outcome: Model accuracy when text prompts conflict with the visual cue, and effect of Chain-of-Thought
evidence.effect: Overall accuracy dropped from 75% to 46% versus the visual-only condition when an inconsistent textual claim was paired with the lesion contour. CoT was associated with further degradation.
evidence.quote: (iii) When an overlaid lesion contour is paired with an inconsistent textual claim, the textual prompt overrides the correct visual cue: overall accuracy drops from 75% to 46% relative to the visual-only condition, and Chain-of-Thought (CoT) reasoning is associated with further degradation rather than self-correction.

evidence.title: Language Models as Interfaces, Not Oracles: A Hybrid LLM-ML System for Pediatric Appendicitis
evidence.outcome: Robustness of end-to-end LLM diagnostic performance to sentence-order permutation of narratives
evidence.effect: End-to-end LLMs showed unstable sensitivity-specificity trade-offs and greater degradation under narrative reordering than the hybrid ClaMPAPP system.
evidence.quote: End-to-end LLMs showed unstable sensitivity-specificity trade-offs and greater degradation under narrative reordering.

evidence.title: Physiology-Aware CNN and Zero-Shot Multimodal LLMs for ECG Image Classification: A Comparative Study
evidence.outcome: LLM sensitivity to ECG image rendering (grid vs grid-free) across repeated runs
evidence.effect: PR-AUC improved slightly with a grid-based calibration background compared with grid-free ECGs; discrimination remained near chance overall.
evidence.quote: The PR-AUC improved slightly when ECGs used a grid-based calibration background compared with the grid-free ECGs.

evidence.title: EHR-Complex: Benchmarking Medical Agents for Complex Clinical Reasoning
evidence.outcome: Output consistency across repeated runs (Pass^k) of LLM agents on EHR tasks
evidence.effect: Pass^k consistency drops below 50% for nearly all evaluated models at k=4; top model reached only 62.3% exact-match accuracy.
evidence.quote: Pass^k consistency drops below 50% for nearly all evaluated models at k=4, exposing broad stochastic fragility.

evidence.title: Bad company corrupts good morals: Understanding and Measuring Narrative-Induced Moral Reasoning Degradation in LLMs
evidence.outcome: Moral reasoning accuracy of LLMs after prolonged negative narrative exposure versus baseline
evidence.effect: Negative narrative exposure degraded moral accuracy across multiple LLMs, with average drops of 12%-31%, worse in ambiguous scenarios and those involving vulnerable individuals; first-person narratives had stronger effects.
evidence.quote: First, negative narrative exposure degrades moral accuracy across multiple LLMs, with average drops of 12%-31%, especially in ambiguous scenarios and those involving vulnerable individuals.

evidence.title: Evaluating LLM Robustness Under Domain-Specific Prompt Perturbations in Public Health Applications
evidence.outcome: LLM accuracy and prediction flips under misinformation framing and layperson rewriting perturbations
evidence.effect: MF degrades accuracy by 7.2 pp on average with prediction flip rates of 9-38 percent, even when claims are labelled unsupported; LR causes only 1.4 pp degradation.
evidence.quote: Experiments show that MF degrades accuracy by 7.2 pp on average with prediction flip rates of 9-38 percent, even when claims are explicitly labelled as unsupported; LR causes only 1.4 pp degradation.

evidence.title: Trivial Prompt Reframing Bypasses Safety Guardrails in Googleś MedGemma-4B
evidence.outcome: Robustness of model behavior under paraphrased/reframed inputs and repeated runs
evidence.effect: ASR shifted substantially by reframing (29.0% baseline to 53.1% under exam framing); topic drove robustness (drug-interaction 83.2% vs emergency 4.7%).
evidence.quote: Robustness is dominated by topic: the drug-interaction guardrail is nearly absent (83.2% ASR) while the emergency-deferral guardrail is strong (4.7%) -- and the authority framing is the only attack that breaches it.

evidence.title: MamaBench: Benchmarking LLM Robustness in Maternal and Child Health Diagnosis through Counterfactual Clinical Perturbation
evidence.outcome: Gap between base accuracy and robust accuracy under counterfactual clinical perturbation
evidence.effect: Base accuracy overstates robust accuracy by 16-28 percentage points in every model; residual BTR of 20% with EA-RAG.
evidence.quote: Across eight configurations of four frontier LLMs, base accuracy overstates robust accuracy by 16-28 percentage points in every model.

evidence.title: Evaluating medical AI under missing information: same-provider judges and human raters change apparent safety
evidence.outcome: Model safety when final user turn is truncated (missing information), knowledge versus calibration
evidence.effect: MedQA accuracy high with option-order effects within +/-5-point equivalence for three of four models, indicating the safety gap under missing information is calibration, not knowledge.
evidence.quote: A closed-ended MedQA anchor confirms accuracy is high and option-order effects are within a +/-5-point equivalence region for three of four models, so the safety gap is about calibration, not knowledge.
evidence.sample_unit: HealthBench conversations (50-item subsample for clinician rating)

evidence.title: Why LLMs Give In: Conversational Factors and Reasoning Behind Medical Sycophancy
evidence.outcome: Model susceptibility to user pushback and framing variations (role, evidence, structure)
evidence.effect: Sycophancy nearly three times more common when users challenge an answer already given than when the false claim is in the initial query; higher for users presented as physicians or medical students.
evidence.quote: Medical sycophancy is nearly three times more common when users challenge an answer the model has already given than when the false claim appears in the initial query.

evidence.title: Evaluating Counterfactual Sensitivity to Patient Information in Medication-Safety Reasoning
evidence.outcome: LLM accuracy on medication-safety questions when patient information is counterfactually changed
evidence.effect: All 28 models performed worse on counterfactual questions; mean accuracy fell from 63.6% to 45.1%. Rationales often acknowledged the change, but final answers kept the prior safety judgment.
evidence.quote: Across 28 medical-specific, general, and proprietary LLMs, every model performs worse on counterfactual questions, with mean accuracy falling from 63.6\% to 45.1\%.

evidence.title: When Calibration Depends on the Scoring Rule: Quantized Biomedical LLM Classification
evidence.outcome: Accuracy sensitivity to prompt template choice across precisions
evidence.effect: Prompt choice changed mean accuracy across precisions by 2.9 to 17.8 percentage points between the two primary templates.
evidence.quote: Between them, prompt choice changes mean accuracy across precisions by 2.9 to 17.8 percentage points.
evidence.sample_unit: test sentences (medical abstract sentences, five-class classification)

evidence.title: An Agentic AI Framework Overcomes Fundamental Limitations of Large Language Models for Glaucoma Detection from Fundus Photography
evidence.outcome: Run-to-run reproducibility of LLM glaucoma classification, measured by kappa across repeated runs
evidence.effect: LLM-alone Gemini 2.5 Flash varied stochastically between runs (kappa as low as -0.01); the agentic workflow raised consistency to kappa up to 0.96.
evidence.quote: Run-to-run consistency rose from near-random (kappa as low as -0.01) to near-perfect (kappa up to 0.96).

evidence.title: TAF-MED: Multi-Turn Safety Refusal Collapse in LLMs Under Declared Self-Treatment Intent
evidence.outcome: Model-ranking stability between first-turn unsafe rate and multi-turn collapse rate
evidence.effect: Four of 28 model pairs reversed order between initial unsafe and collapse rates.
evidence.quote: Four of 28 model pairs reversed order between initial unsafe and collapse rates.

evidence.title: Inhibitory Attention for Clinical Long-Context Reasoning: Characterizing and Mitigating Lost-in-the-Middle Effects in EHR Processing
evidence.outcome: LLM accuracy on EHR instructions by position of relevant information within long context
evidence.effect: 21.9 percentage-point gap between peak accuracy (59.5%) and trough accuracy (37.6%); 67.8% of reference answers fall inside the trough (10th-90th percentile of the EHR timeline).
evidence.quote: Across 2,196 instruction-response pairs and six language models, we observe a 21.9 percentage-point gap between peak accuracy (59.5%, 95% CI [46.3, 71.0], 20-30% decile) and trough accuracy (37.6% [23.2, 52.5] at 70-80%); 67.8% of reference answers fall between the 10th and 90th percentiles of the EHR timeline, inside the CLitM trough.

evidence.title: TSWAP: A Multilingual Retrieval-Augmented Thai Wellness Advisor
evidence.outcome: Test-retest reproducibility of production QA cases
evidence.effect: 91.1% test-retest pass over 259 cases.
evidence.quote: We release the first Thai traditional-medicine/wellness retrieval benchmark (50 questions with gold document IDs; Recall@5 = 0.88), production QA logs (91.1% test-retest pass over 259 cases), and a 71-question frontier no-retrieval probe showing what each grounding pillar contributes: without the safety prompt the backend model family produced a full drug-dosing schedule and complied with out-of-scope requests, and without the knowledge base it produced zero verifiable provider recommendations.

evidence.title: Neurosymbolic Alignment for Physiologically-Safe Clinical Language Models
evidence.outcome: Safety score (CSS) under synthetic EHR-style input noise
evidence.effect: 84.2% CSS retained under synthetic EHR-style noise, versus 90.8% CSS on clean benchmark inputs (a drop of about 6.6 pp).
evidence.quote: Under synthetic EHR-style noise, 84.2% CSS is retained.

evidence.title: Right Diagnoses, Decorative Reasoning:A Perturbation Audit of Medical Chain-of-Thought
evidence.outcome: Chain-of-thought response to clinically motivated input and chain perturbations
evidence.effect: Chain-Decoupling Rate 72.9% panel-wide on clinically meaningful destructive edits; chain corruption leaves accuracy unchanged; removing CoT prompting does not reduce accuracy.
evidence.quote: the Chain-Decoupling Rate (CDR; chain does not register the edit and the answer does not flip) is 72.9% panel-wide on clinically meaningful destructive edits, chain corruption leaves accuracy unchanged, and removing CoT prompting does not reduce accuracy.
evidence.sample_unit: LLMs evaluated on four medical QA benchmarks

evidence.title: When Patients Cut In: Extending Clinical Conversational AI Safety to Interruptions
evidence.outcome: Preservation of clinically required content after simulated patient interruptions in voice-agent transcripts
evidence.effect: Competitive FAQ interruption produced 30/30 provision-coverage failures for all four models (Wilson 95% CI 88.6-100.0%); baseline 0/30 for three models, 4/30 for Llama.
evidence.quote: Rankings differ across cells, and competitive FAQ interruption produced 30/30 provision-coverage failures for all four models (Wilson 95% CI: 88.6-100.0%; baseline 0/30 for three, 4/30 for Llama).
evidence.sample_unit: simulated interruption conversation transcripts (30 per condition in reported cells)

evidence.title: Investigating Linear Probe Robustness to Linguistic Register, Medical Specialty, and Corpus Shifts in Medical QA
evidence.outcome: Linear probe AUROC change under register, specialty, and corpus shifts
evidence.effect: Truth direction largely robust to writing style (mean Δ_register ≈ 0.10 AUROC) and specialty (Δ ≈ 0.03), but degrades by 0.12 AUROC on MMLU-medical and 0.21 on MedMCQA.
evidence.quote: Probing four open-weight LLMs (2--8B), we find that the truth direction is largely robust to writing style (mean $Δ_\text{register} \approx 0.10$ AUROC on held-out facts) and to medical specialty ($Δ_\text{specialty} \approx 0.03$), but degrades unevenly across corpora: by $0.12$ AUROC on MMLU-medical and by $0.21$ on MedMCQA, roughly twice the register gap.
evidence.sample_unit: MedQA entries (each rewritten into four styles)

evidence.title: PhysioBench: A Unified Benchmark for Physiological Signal Question Answering
evidence.outcome: Sensitivity of model performance to question formulation (input wording variation)
evidence.effect: Performance remains sensitive to question formulation; no model achieved consistently strong performance across modalities and tasks. No numbers given in the abstract.
evidence.quote: The incorporation of natural language supports unified prediction across tasks, although performance remains sensitive to question formulation.

evidence.title: LLMs Anchor on Chief Complaint and Fail to Integrate Evidence in Sequential Clinical Triage
evidence.outcome: LLM triage sensitivity to input variation via controlled perturbations and prompting interventions
evidence.effect: Controlled perturbations showed labels at every checkpoint were anchored on the chief complaint exchanges. Prompting interventions failed to lift the plateau.
evidence.quote: Controlled perturbations show that the label at every checkpoint is anchored on the chief complaint exchanges, and prompting interventions fail to lift this plateau.

evidence.title: Misaligned Clinical Risk Classification and Cost Asymmetry in Open-Weight Large Language Models
evidence.outcome: Decision sensitivity to phrasing of cost instructions across three phrasings
evidence.effect: Only 2 of 12 model-phrasings showed both opposing responses to increasing FN versus FP costs and cost-correct ordering.
evidence.quote: Only 2 of 12 model-phrasings showed both opposing responses to increasing FN versus FP costs and cost-correct ordering.

evidence.title: How Can I Stay Healthy? – Benchmarking Large Language Models for Personalized and Biomarker-Based Intervention Recommendations
evidence.outcome: LLM response robustness to prompt variability across combinatorial test cases
evidence.effect: LLMs responded positively to more concrete system-prompt instructions but remained vulnerable to overall prompt variability (1,000 test cases built combinatorially).
evidence.quote: LLMs respond positively to more concrete instructions in the system prompt but remain vulnerable to overall prompt variability.

evidence.title: Unmasking True Clinical Competence: The Importance of Adaptive and Open-Ended Evaluation for Large Language Models in Cardiology
evidence.outcome: Accuracy after modifying critical clinical parameters in questions
evidence.effect: Modified MC accuracy fell from 93.9% to 66.7% for answers and to 71.2% for reasoning (both p<0.001); answer-reasoning concordance fell from 93.9% to 66.7% (p<0.001).
evidence.quote: For modified MC questions, accuracy decreased significantly (answers: 93.9% to 66.7%; reasoning: 93.9% to 71.2%; both p<0.001), as well as answer-reasoning concordance (93.9% to 66.7%, p<0.001).

evidence.title: Beyond Benchmarks: Towards Robust Artificial Intelligence Bone Segmentation in Socio-Technical Systems
evidence.outcome: Segmentation accuracy variation across voxel size, orientation, and osteosynthesis or pathology
evidence.effect: Segmentation accuracy varied by up to 25% depending on voxel size, bone orientation, and patient conditions such as osteosynthesis or pathology; metallic osteosynthesis and anatomical complexity significantly degraded results.
evidence.quote: We show that segmentation accuracy varies by up to 25% depending on socio-technical factors such as voxel size, bone orientation, and patient conditions such as osteosynthesis or pathology.

evidence.title: LLM Reasoning Does Not Protect Against Clinical Cognitive Biases - An Evaluation Using BiasMedQA
evidence.outcome: LLM accuracy on clinical vignettes with cognitive-bias-inducing input framing, base versus reasoning models
evidence.effect: Reasoning did not consistently prevent cognitive bias; reasoning models had better overall performance (OR 4.0 Llama, OR 3.6 Qwen), but Llama reasoning increased vulnerability to frequency bias (OR 0.6) and recency bias (OR 0.5).
evidence.quote: In neither of the two models, reasoning capabilities were able to consistently prevent cognitive bias, although both reasoning models achieved better overall performance compared to their respective base model (OR 4.0 for Llama-3.3-70B, OR 3.6 for Qwen3-32B).

evidence.title: Comparative Analysis of Multimodal Large Language Models GPT-4o and o1 vs Clinicians in Clinical Case Challenge Questions
evidence.outcome: Reproducibility of correct answers across five repeated trials
evidence.effect: Across five trials, GPT-4o and o1 provided the correct answer 5/5 times in 86.2% and 90.7% of cases, respectively, indicating some run-to-run inconsistency.
evidence.quote: Across five trials, GPT-4o and o1 provided the correct answer 5/5 times in 86.2% and 90.7% of the cases, respectively.

evidence.title: Bridging the Semantic Gaps: Improving MVQA Consistency with LLM-Augmented Question Sets
evidence.outcome: Answer consistency of medical VQA models across paraphrased versions of the same question
evidence.effect: Models flip answers when the same query is rephrased. Fine-tuning on LLM-augmented paraphrases raised mean answer accuracy by 19.4% and TAR-SC (accuracy plus across-paraphrase agreement) by 11.6%.
evidence.quote: We confront a critical yet under-studied weakness of Medical Visual Question Answering (MVQA): models often flip their answers when clinicians phrase the same diagnostic query differently.

evidence.title: Evaluating the Impact of Authoritative and Subjective Cues on Large Language Model Reliability for Clinical Inquiries: An Experimental Study
evidence.outcome: LLM accuracy on a clinical question under neutral versus misleading prompt framings
evidence.effect: Baseline accuracy 100% for all models; fell to 45% with incorrect self-recall prompts and 1% with authoritative prompts; Cramér's V = 0.75, P < .001.
evidence.quote: However, accuracy significantly decreased in conditions with misleading cues, dropping to 45% with self-recall prompts and 1% with authoritative prompts.
evidence.sample_unit: test runs (5 models x 5 scenarios x 10 repetitions)

evidence.title: Performance of Artificial Intelligence and Large Language Models (LLMs) on Neurosurgical Board Examinations Across Text and Visual Modalities
evidence.outcome: Accuracy change when withholding history, physical exam, or lab components of clinical vignettes
evidence.effect: Removing history reduced accuracy by 19.3%; withholding physical exam or lab data reduced it by 6.0% and 5.9%.
evidence.quote: Ablation experiments showed that removal of history produced the largest decline in accuracy (19.3% reduction), while withholding physical exam or lab data produced smaller effects (6.0% and 5.9%).

evidence.title: Recognizing "Conformity Bias" in Large Language Models: A New Risk for Clinical Use
evidence.outcome: Correct response rate after successive probing questions suggesting incorrect treatments (conformity bias)
evidence.effect: Correct rates after repeated probing: 25% GPT-4o, 10% Gemini-1.5 Flash, 0% Claude-3 Haiku, 25% GPT-o1 (P < 0.001); conformity to incorrect suggestions increased with repeated probing.
evidence.quote: Correct response rates after successive probing questions were alarmingly low: 25% (GPT-4o), 10% (Gemini-1.5 Flash), 0% (Claude-3 Haiku), and 25% (GPT-o1) (P < 0.001).

evidence.title: LLMs Can Do Medical Harm: Stress-Testing Clinical Decisions Under Social Pressure
evidence.outcome: Harmful decision rate across social-pressure prompt variations versus neutral control
evidence.effect: Authority or responsibility-transfer framings produced the most harmful responses; control prompts the fewest (mitigated 8.3–9.6%; unmitigated 14.3–16.0%; p<0.001).
evidence.quote: When exposed to social pressure, models behaved predictably but unevenly: prompts framed as authority or responsibility transfer generated the most harmful responses, whereas control prompts, neutral and pressure-free, produced the fewest (mitigated 8.3–9.6%; unmitigated 14.3–16.0%; χ  2 p < 0.001).

evidence.title: Failure-Aware Robustness Evaluation of Deep Learning Models for Tuberculosis Detection Under Real-World Chest X-Ray Degradation
evidence.outcome: Model performance and calibration under synthetically degraded chest X-ray inputs
evidence.effect: All models showed statistically significant degradation; motion blur reduced sensitivity by up to 21%; expected calibration error rose from about 0.04 to over 0.10 under degradation.
evidence.quote: Motion blur was the most detrimental artifacts, causing sensitivity reductions of up to 21%.

evidence.title: Comparative Accuracy of Large Language Models for CPT Coding Assignments from Surgical Procedure Notes
evidence.outcome: Run-to-run consistency of LLM CPT code outputs across three repeated queries
evidence.effect: Gemini had highest consistency (72.7% identical outputs across runs); Claude 63.6%; complex multi-component procedures showed greater inter-run variance.
evidence.quote: Consistency did not correlate with accuracy: Gemini demonstrated the highest run-to-run consistency (72.7% identical outputs across runs) despite lower benchmark alignment, while Claude showed greater variance (63.6%) yet superior accuracy.
evidence.sample_unit: orthopedic procedure notes with surgeon-labeled benchmark CPT codes

evidence.title: Artificial Intelligence in Clinical Practice: Evaluating Chatbot Performance on Board-Level Questions in Geriatrics
evidence.outcome: Consistency of model answers across two repeated attempts on the same questions
evidence.effect: Consistency was 96.3% for GPT-4o, 95.0% for Grok-3, 90.7% for Copilot and 81.3% for Gemini, so repeated-run answers were not fully reproducible.
evidence.quote: GPT-4o exhibited the highest consistency (96.3%), followed by Grok-3 (95.0%), Copilot (90.7%), and Gemini (81.3%).

evidence.title: When Agentic LLMs Trust Poisoned Tools: Vulnerability of Clinical LLMs to Adversarial Guidelines
evidence.outcome: Sensitivity of model choices to option order (presentation bias)
evidence.effect: Models favored the first option in 72.7% of decisions, shifting accuracy from 36.7% to 82.3% depending on sham position.
evidence.quote: Choices were dominated by presentation bias: models favored the first option in 72.7% of decisions, shifting accuracy from 36.7% to 82.3% depending on sham position.

evidence.title: Beyond Benchmarks: Dynamic, Automatic And Systematic Red-Teaming Agents For Trustworthy Medical Language Models
evidence.outcome: Answer stability of previously correct MedQA responses under dynamic adversarial mutation of test cases
evidence.effect: 94% of previously correct answers failed dynamic robustness tests despite median MedQA accuracy above 80%; HealthBench failure rates exceeded 70% for top-tier models.
evidence.quote: Despite median MedQA accuracy exceeding 80%, 94% of previously correct answers failed our dynamic robustness tests.

evidence.title: Stochastic Incompleteness: A Predictability Taxonomy for Clinical AI Deployment
evidence.outcome: Trial-to-trial output consistency and completeness of clinical summaries across repeated runs
evidence.effect: Accuracy and predictability were independent (r = -0.24, p = 0.56, N = 8). LAD occlusion appeared in only 22% of Llama 4 Scout summaries (Variance Ratio 7.46); Llama 4 Maverick VR 2.64.
evidence.quote: LAD occlusion, a critical clinical finding in STEMI cases, appears in only 22% of Llama 4 Scout summaries despite the model correctly identifying it when directly queried.

evidence.title: Obedience to Unsafe Clinical Instructions: How Large Language Models Respond to Authority Cues
evidence.outcome: LLM output safety under perturbed prompts with social-pressure framing
evidence.effect: Harmful decisions varied by pressure condition; authority and responsibility-transfer cues elicited highest harmful compliance, control lowest, with mitigation preserving the pattern.
evidence.quote: Across all conditions, authority and responsibility-transfer cues elicited the highest harmful compliance, and control prompts the lowest; mitigation reduced rates but preserved this pattern.

evidence.title: Privacy-PreservingLLM Middleware in LIS: Edge-Computing for Coagulation InterpretationUnder High-Dimensional Noise
evidence.outcome: Guideline concordance accuracy under injected semantic and lexical input noise, versus rule-based baseline
evidence.effect: LLM-RAG kept 97.00% guideline concordance accuracy under 30% semantic and 15% lexical noise; rule-based baseline fell to 10.00%. Critical violation rate 1.50%.
evidence.quote: The proposed LLM-RAG middleware demonstrated exceptional robustness,maintaining a Guideline Concordance Accuracy (\((ACC_{gc})\)) of 97.00%under high-dimensional noise, whereas the traditional rule-basedbaseline collapsed to 10.00%.

evidence.title: MedClarify: An information-seeking AI agent for medical diagnosis with case-specific follow-up questions
evidence.outcome: LLM diagnostic behavior when patient cases are incomplete or missing information
evidence.effect: Current LLMs often yield multiple, similarly likely diagnoses, especially when patient cases are incomplete or relevant information is missing; no numbers given for this result.
evidence.quote: In our experiments, we first demonstrate the limitations of current LLMs in medical reasoning, which often yield multiple, similarly likely diagnoses, especially when patient cases are incomplete or relevant information for diagnosis is missing.

evidence.title: not-yet-known not-yet-known not-yet-known unknown Evaluating the accuracy of large language models on ESGO/ESTRO/ESP guidelines for cervical cancer: are large language models reliable assistants in clinical practice?
evidence.outcome: Intra-model response consistency across repeated submissions of the same question
evidence.effect: Response consistency varied significantly: ChatGPT-4.0 and DeepSeek-R1 differed from Gemini-2.0 (p=0.034 and p=0.044, respectively).
evidence.quote: Response consistency varied significantly, with ChatGPT-4.0 and DeepSeek-R1 showing differences from Gemini-2.0 (p=0.034 and p=0.044, respectively).

evidence.title: Clinical Note Comparison and Data Retrieval Via Embedding Vectors: Model Selection, Metrics, and Convergence
evidence.outcome: Embedding model detection of direction of semantic change under controlled text perturbations
evidence.effect: On average models detected direction of change correctly, but case-level performance varied; Qwen3-Embedding-8B had zero directional errors while multilingual-E5-large erred in 13.8% of cases.

evidence.quote: Across 11 model configurations, mean accuracy falls from 71.1% on original questions to 38.0% under focused misleading context, with 51.5% attack success.

evidence.title: ConfidentNeuro: Conformal Prediction-Based Uncertainty Quantification for Hallucination Risk Scoring in LLM-Assisted Alzheimer's Clinical Decision Support
evidence.outcome: Model confidence change under eight input perturbations relative to semantic disruption
evidence.effect: Confidence barely changed, staying around 0.56–0.62, despite a twofold variation in semantic disruption, indicating systemic failure in self-assessment.
evidence.quote: Under perturbation audit across eight input modifications, confidence barely changed, staying around 0.56–0.62, despite a twofold variation in semantic disruption.

evidence.title: Agent Role Structure and Operating Characteristics in Large Language Model Clinical Classification: A Comparative Study of Specialist and Deliberative Multi-Agent Protocols
evidence.outcome: Sensitivity of classification performance to prompt/protocol structure and feature assignment

evidence.title: Drug-drug interaction identification using large language models

evidence.title: Automatic speech recognition alters diagnostic error and biomarker validity in AI-based dementia speech assessment

evidence.quote: These findings show that automated transcription does not simply introduce random noise into the speech-based assessment but it can systematically change clinical error profiles and biomarker estimates.

evidence.title: A Multi-Agent clinical pre-consultation system for structuring noisy patient reported information into clinical reports and AI-ready data

evidence.title: Trustworthy agentic genomics through versioned skill libraries

evidence.title: Clinical Reliability and Consistency of Large Language Models in Prosthodontics: An Expert Evaluation of ChatGPT and Gemini

evidence.quote: Gemini showed better response stability with a concordance coefficient of κ = 0.62 compared with κ = 0.46 for ChatGPT.

evidence.title: Artificial Intelligence-Enabled Cardiac Function Estimation from Phone Videos of Echocardiograms

evidence.title: Performance evaluation and benchmarking across 16 large language models on a comprehensive real-world emergency department triage data set
evidence.outcome: Reproducibility of LLM triage outputs across repeated runs
evidence.effect: Reproducibility testing revealed substantial variability in 23% of cases, indicating non-deterministic output behavior.
evidence.quote: Reproducibility testing revealed substantial variability in 23% of cases, indicating non-deterministic output behavior for clinically relevant decisions.

evidence.title: Prompt-engineering improves clinical safety of large language models for opioid equipotency conversion
evidence.outcome: Sensitivity of LLM responses to vignette wording changes

evidence.quote: Vignette wording changes accounted for 76% of within-scenario response variance.

evidence.title: A Systematic Exploration of LLM Behavior for EHR Phenotyping
evidence.outcome: Prediction consistency (Shannon entropy) across prompting strategies and temperature

evidence.quote: Prediction entropy was low overall and driven primarily by phenotype difficulty rather than prompting or temperature.

evidence.title: Reproducibility and Robustness of Large Language Models for Mobility Functional Status Extraction
evidence.outcome: Stability of LLM extraction across repeated runs and paraphrased prompts
evidence.effect: Increasing temperature generally degrades agreement; prompt paraphrasing can substantially reduce stability, with particularly large drops for the MoE model.
evidence.quote: Results show that increasing temperature generally degrades agreement, but the magnitude depends on model and task; furthermore, prompt paraphrasing can substantially reduce stability, with particularly large drops for the MoE model.

evidence.title: Structured retrieval closes the gap between low-cost and frontier clinical language models
evidence.outcome: NIHSS scoring error under context stress (length, distractors, information position)

evidence.quote: Structured retrieval reduces mean absolute error (MAE) from 4.58 to 2.96 points relative to non-agentic baselines (mean gain 1.62 MAE points; 95% CI 1.57–1.67; 35% relative reduction), with consistent gains across all 36 stress combinations.

evidence.title: Show Your Work: Verbatim Evidence Requirements and Automated Assessment for Large Language Models in Biomedical Text Processing
evidence.outcome: Label reproducibility across three repeated runs per abstract
evidence.effect: Fleiss' kappa across repetitions ranged 0.829 to 0.969, indicating stable labels.
evidence.quote: Labels were stable across repetitions (Fleiss’ kappa 0.829 to 0.969).

evidence.title: Performance Characteristics of Reasoning Large Language Models for Evidence Extraction from Clinical Genomics Literature
evidence.outcome: Sensitivity of PS4 counting concordance to prompt refinements across five LLMs
evidence.effect: Prompt refinements improved concordance for most models but reduced performance for Claude Sonnet 4, indicating performance is model- and prompt-dependent.
evidence.quote: Prompt refinements improved concordance for most models but reduced performance for Claude Sonnet 4, indicating model specific prompting may be warranted.

evidence.title: Boards-style benchmarks overestimate prior-chat bias in large language models: a factorial evaluation study
evidence.outcome: Accuracy change after prior-chat distractors across 14 LLMs on MedQA and EHRNoteQA
evidence.effect: MedQA multiple-choice: significant accuracy drops in 13 of 14 models, averaging 15.0 percentage points. Smaller effects for conversational distractors and free-response. EHR task: average decreases under 2 points, significant in a minority of models.
evidence.quote: In this setting, insertion of this user message led to significant accuracy decreases in 13 of 14 models, with drops averaging 15·0 percentage points across models.

evidence.title: Understanding Clinical Reasoning Variability in Medical Large Language Models: A Mechanistic Interpretability Study
evidence.outcome: Staging accuracy stability under systematic prompt and case perturbations
evidence.effect: Models showed dramatic reasoning instability, shifting staging accuracy by over 50% based solely on prompt format, and generating definitive staging in clinically insufficient scenarios.
evidence.quote: We find models exhibit dramatic reasoning instability, shifting staging accuracy by over 50% based solely on prompt format, or generating definitive staging in clinically insufficient scenarios.

evidence.title: Pathology’s Last Exam: Stress-Testing Diagnostic Reasoning and Safety in Large Language Models
evidence.outcome: Model behavior on adversarial, biologically implausible 'mix-up' pathology cases
evidence.effect: Models frequently failed to detect biological contradictions and confidently diagnosed nonsensical mix-up cases instead of refusing them; no numeric rate given in abstract.
evidence.quote: Models frequently failed to detect biological contradictions, confidently diagnosing nonsensical “mix-up” cases rather than refusing them.

evidence.title: FHIRBench: Benchmarking FHIR Clinical Data Serialization Strategies for Large Language Models
evidence.outcome: LLM output quality sensitivity to input serialization format across models
evidence.effect: Serialization significantly changed quality on both evaluation layers; significant Model x Serializer interaction (Friedman p = 0.0009), with best format differing by model (GPT-5.4 favoring Raw JSON, others compressed formats).
evidence.quote: Third, a significant Model × Serializer interaction (Friedman p = 0.0009) precludes universal format recommendations, with GPT-5.4 favoring Raw JSON while Claude and open-weight models favor compressed formats.

evidence.title: Does Model Compression Amplify Clinical Bias? A Subgroup Fairness Audit of Quantized ICU Risk Models on MIMIC-IV
evidence.outcome: quantization robustness to implausible inputs
evidence.effect: Naive dynamic quantization collapsed AUROC to 0.500 because implausible vitals/labs dominated activation-quantization range; plausibility filter recovered AUROC to 0.699.
evidence.quote: We report two methodological findings alongside the fairness results: (1) naive per-tensor dynamic quantization collapsed AUROC to chance level (0.500) due to a small number of physiologically implausible raw vitals/labs readings dominating the activation-quantization range– fixed at the source with a documented plausibility filter, recovering AUROC to 0.699; and (2) diffing an out-of-fold baseline against in-sample-evaluated compressed models produces a spurious ”compression improves fairness” artifact, corrected with a sameprotocol baseline.

evidence.title: Agentic-TimesFM-AKI: A Dual LLM–Time Series Framework for Predicting Drug-Induced Acute Kidney Injury with Privacy-Preserving Synthetic Data
evidence.outcome: Model robustness to input/schema formatting variation
evidence.effect: Framework showed structural formatting fragility and domain shift on out-of-distribution EHR data.
evidence.quote: While the dual-model framework provides highly accurate and interpretable AKI alerts on familiar schema cohorts, it suffers from structural formatting fragility and domain shift.

evidence.title: An Agentic OODA Framework for Transparent End to End Clinical Decision Support

evidence.quote: In particular, Large Language Model (LLM) based systems often exhibit variability between different runs on the same input, which makes them unsuitable for safety-critical clinical applications.

evidence.title: Architectural Safety Mechanisms for Multi-Agent Clinical LLM Systems Under Knowledge Base Distribution Shift

evidence.title: Intent Drift in LLM-Assisted BCI Communication: An In-Silico Benchmark Under Simulated Decoder Corruption

evidence.quote: Drift rose steeply with decoder error, from 2.2% at no error to 60.3% at the most severe level tested (odds ratio 2.30 per 10-percentage-point increase)-a stress-test ceiling, not an expected real-world rate.

evidence.title: RoMIA: A Framework for Creating Robust Medical Imaging AI

evidence.quote: Models produced by RoMIA show 3-5% improvement in robust accuracy, suggesting that the proposed methods can be a useful step towards enabling the adoption of ANNs in medical imaging applications.

evidence.title: Tissue contamination challenges the credibility of machine learning models in real world digital pathology

evidence.quote: Every model showed performance degradation in response to one or more tissue contaminants.

evidence.title: Evaluating ChatGPT-4 in Otolaryngology–Head and Neck Surgery Board Examination using the CVSA Model

evidence.title: Assessing generalizability of an AI-based visual test for cervical cancer screening
